title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock, who have a KU Alumni license plate numbered 7007, were stopped twice after automated Flock cameras flagged their minivan as possibly stolen. A stolen GMC pickup had a temporary tag with the same number, 7007, but a different plate background. The first stop was in Colwich, Kansas, where an officer quickly realized the error. About a month later, police in Catoosa, Oklahoma, pulled them over at a casino, pointed guns at them, and handcuffed Matthew before realizing the mistake.

Kansas duplicates plate numbers across more than 100 designs, about half specialty plates, and Flock cameras read only letters and numbers, not plate type. Wichita police Captain Casey Slaughter said alerts alone are not enough for a stop, but once a stolen tag is confirmed, officers have little choice. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit plate numbers to avoid duplicates. The Spurlocks plan to keep their 14 year old plate and are no longer worried because the stolen vehicle entry has expired.
